data.name: Rukmangada
data.gender_notes: Rukmangada is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Rukma' meaning gold or golden and 'Angada' meaning wheel. The name Rukmangada carries the meaning “Golden Wheel” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rukmangada usually hope their child will grow to embody golden wheel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Rukmangada belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Golden Wheel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rukmangada total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rukmangada holds significant cultural importance in Hindu mythology. Rukmangada was the name of a monkey king or vanara, who is believed to have played an essential role in the epic Ramayana by aiding Lord Rama in defeating the demon king Ravana and rescuing his wife Sita. His name signifies power, strength, and the golden era of righteous rule.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, Rukmangada's name is thought to symbolize the power and magnificence of devotion, strength, and loyalty to dharma (cosmic law or duty). The name can serve as an inspiration for individuals seeking to live a righteous and virtuous life, embodying the qualities of strength, loyalty, and devotion to their beliefs or spiritual path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rukmangada: Radiant as the thread of gold in the celestial loom, embodiment of divine grace and prosperity.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads, but widely used in Hindu mythology and literature.

historical_references.reference: Rukmangada, a celebrated king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic, the Ramayana. He is known for his hospitality towards Lord Rama, who stayed in his kingdom during his exile. Rukmangada's city, Ayodhya, was Lord Rama's ancestral home before his exile.

Rukmangada, also known as Indradyumna, was a king of the Vatsa dynasty mentioned in the Indian Buddhist text, the Mahavamsa. He is notable for building the famous Buddhist monument, the Lanka Buddha Vihara, on the island of Lanka.
